authorityOrder.scope: Legion-wide architecture, ownership boundaries, global invariants, orchestration, authority, and effect semantics
Accepted native-Rust product topology, runtime, client, Blueprint, release, and state target
Ordered migration, qualification, hard-cut, and cleanup gates
Capability and entrypoint method semantics, constrained by the root SSOT
Delegated routing and independent Completion Validation method, constrained by the root SSOT

rules: A capability is domain, workflow, or context expertise; an entrypoint is an explicit compatibility or orchestration surface.
Domain metadata is optional grouping only and never a routing hierarchy.
Natural-language routing selects from the compact canonical catalog; deterministic runtime validates selected identifiers and explicit aliases but does not interpret prose.
Only entrypoints carry target mappings; capability identity never statically grants authority.
Package-internal, host-capability, project-overlay, and historical-evidence references remain explicitly classified; project overlays are optional and declare absence behavior.

workGraphAndAuthority.owner: Legion Rust core with producing-capability routine judgment
rules: A work unit declares capabilities, operations, effects, dependencies, and authority only where required.
Operations, effects, and authority are independent axes; execute does not imply Alchemist and judgment alone does not imply Sage.
Sage handles material unresolved adjudication, Alchemist controlled bounded transformation when policy or risk requires it, and Oracle is independent read-only Completion Validation.
Covenant is optional, bounded, advisory, and has no effect or disposition authority.

policyAndEffects.owner: Arcane policy data plus Legion Rust evaluator
rules: Effect intent is explicit and Arcane evaluates it immediately before the effect.
Legion-owned algorithms do not invoke Node, Python, shell scripts, or another Legion runtime.
A target repository's compiler, browser, scanner, VCS, Node, Python, or Cargo is an intentional typed external-project-tool effect, not a Legion runtime dependency.

No shell command string is accepted for a typed external-tool request; executable identity, bounded arguments, timeout, output cap, cancellation/process-tree control, policy outcome, and receipt are required.

Every bounded external effect has a receipt bound to the provider, repository binding, denominator, command identity, timing, status, output artifacts, environment keys, sandbox/process-tree evidence, tool qualification, and normalized provider result.
A receipt never converts unavailable, blocked, partial, missing, invalid, or incomplete evidence into pass.
Provider reconciliation requires one terminal receipt for every selected provider, no unplanned or duplicate receipt, correct binding and denominator, and visible coverage gaps.

audit.owner: Legion Rust core; Audit owns systematic evaluation methodology
rules: Audit freezes repository binding, scope, selected provider set, denominator, and provider plan before execution.
Audit plans, executes, reconciles, and reports deterministic providers; candidate generators cannot close their own findings.
Every selected provider reconciles to evidence or a typed degradation; incomplete coverage is never a clean audit claim.
Audit status, quality gate, process execution state, and independent Completion Validation are separate verdicts.

research.owner: Legion Rust core; Research owns evidence-routing method
rules: Research freezes a route before effects, records approval receipts before stage-two work, and emits a route-scoped evidence artifact and terminal receipt.
A search hit, snippet, AI summary, provider answer, or NotebookLM answer is a lead, never ledger evidence; evidence requires an opened source and locator.
Atomic claims preserve source links, dates, scope, contradiction, uncertainty, and confidence ceilings; a claim cannot exceed its bound proof.
When required live retrieval is unavailable, Research reports truthful UNPROVEN/typed degradation and does not guess.

reviewAndCompletion.owner: Legion Rust core for review protocol; Oracle for independent Completion Validation
rules: Review uses bounded judgment packets with identified evidence and omitted material; unknown remains an honest verdict.
Oracle Completion Validation is source-first, independent, read-only semantic assurance before successful delivery.
Completion Validation reconstructs raw current scope, inspects changed source and consumers, may read tests to understand behavior, and never runs or reruns tests.
Oracle returns only PASS or BLOCK, reports concrete safety/behavior/data-loss defects, does not author remediation or durable review artifacts, and permits at most one repair/recheck loop.
Claim levels are inventory, source, runtime, product, and release; a claimed level is achieved only by passing the required lower/equal evidence stages.
Missing evidence produces incomplete or unproven, never a clean claim.
Claim proof records retain the evidence objects that satisfy referenced evidence identifiers; missing references are unproven.

blueprintDegradation.owner: Membrane owns context selection/evidence publication; Blueprint owns repository truth; Legion owns only the typed consumer boundary
rules: Blueprint is optional context acceleration and is never a global Audit prerequisite.

When Blueprint is unavailable, execute every applicable non-Blueprint provider, preserve the selected-provider denominator, emit a visible recommendation and exact structural-coverage limits, and retain non-Blueprint results.
Only an operation explicitly marked Blueprint-dependent may return provider-level typed degradation; it cannot abort unrelated work, produce empty success, or surface as a machinery crash.
Legion never walks Blueprint storage, synthesizes a local graph fallback, or modifies Membrane.

migrationInvariants: One machine-installed Rust runtime owns all shipped Legion semantics and executable workflows.
Client-native adapters are mechanical and may not own routing, Audit, Research, Arcane policy, work graphs, receipts, capability semantics, or another Legion ontology.
One reusable client-owned stdio MCP process serves an active client session; there is no idle Legion daemon and no per-tool Legion runtime birth.
Markdown, JSON, YAML, schemas, prompts, lenses, recipes, and rule packs remain declarative assets.
Development-only Node/Python test and build tools remain unless a refreshed source-bound inventory explicitly classifies their deletion.
M0 does not implement a runtime port, modify Membrane, run Cargo, commit, or push.

requiredDownstreamConsumers: M1-M8 implementation dispatch compiled after all M0 contracts converge
